text:
ana-sales: Heads-up: SolsticePay POC started ramping. They're seeing large first-token latency tails (p95 ~750ms) and intermittent 503s when they ramp to ~55 concurrent streams. Can infra/devswarm? cc @peter-eng @rachel-sre @gina-solutions
peter-eng: on it. what's the typical input size and are they using streaming + many parallel requests per session? any sample request id?
ana-sales: their engineer supplied a trace id rp-soli-20240211-14:22:08 and a brief header dump. Inputs are tiny (avg 12 tokens) and they fan out 4x per user session with streaming on. header snippet:

--hdr--
X-Request-Id: rp-soli-20240211-14:22:08
X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 3000
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 5
X-Forwarded-For: 54.203.1.7
User-Agent: SolsticePay/2.0 connector
--end--

rachel-sre: checked cluster: short spike on shard group gpu-qpool-1 at 14:22:10. Logs: 
[2024-02-11T14:22:11Z] WARN serve: batch flush triggered early, batch_size=72, batch_window_target=25ms
[2024-02-11T14:22:11Z] ERROR serve: queue timeout after 90s shard=1 req=rp-soli-20240211-14:22:08 status=503

rachel-sre: also seeing prefix KV cache miss_rate=78% and frequent evictions; their request patterns are high-cardinality small prompts so caching is ineffective currently.

peter-eng: classic small-prompt fanout problem. Two quick config knobs we can flip: 1) per-route max_batch_size=24 and batch_window_ms=8 to avoid huge batches, 2) enable single_item_fastpath for <32-token requests to bypass batching. Also recommend client-side change: reduce concurrent fanout 4->1 per session with short jitter.
gina-solutions: customer is nervous about changing their client right now. can we try server-side mitigations first?
kevin-support: yes, we can push per-route changes to a test route. I'll stage a change: max_batch_size=24, batch_window_ms=8, enable fastpath.
deploy-bot: Route update scheduled: sales/solstice-poc -> apply config (max_batch_size=24, batch_window_ms=8, single_item_fastpath=true) in 30s.
rachel-sre: after the change dashboards show median TTFT reduced from 420ms -> 150ms within 45s, queue depth down ~60%. 503s stopped. Still seeing occasional 429s at burst peaks.
peter-eng: for the 429s we should check their token budget and whether they're hitting global rate limits vs per-route. If they need sustained higher concurrency we can propose a small Dedicated reserved pool or temporary burst credits.
gina-solutions: they asked about cost for Dedicated and burst credits for the pilot. I'll prepare an estimate. We should offer a short trial burst allowance to avoid blocking the demo.
sec-maya: security request: Solstice asked for AWS KMS integration details and an allowlist template. They also want confirmation on SOC2 scope. I can send a short pack but need their internal security contact to fill our questionnaire.
ana-sales: I'll get their sec contact and send the questionnaire. They also asked about warmup/prefill: can Redwood prefill KV cache for their expected prompt prefixes?
rachel-sre: we can do route-level prefill if they provide typical prefixes list. That would cut miss rate dramatically. Also we can enable pre-warming of worker replicas for the test window.
peter-eng: additional option: enable adaptive-batching with lower max_batch_size during burst windows and automatically scale shard count up by 1 for 5 minutes to absorb spikes (if on Dedicated that's trivial; on hosted it's slower — we'd need to open a manual capacity bump).
gina-solutions: let's try this sequence: (1) keep server-side batch caps & fastpath (done), (2) request prefixes from Solstice for prefill (action: Ana), (3) offer 14-day burst credits in the quote (action: Gina), (4) Security pack to customer (action: Maya).
kevin-support: monitoring note: after changes, p95 TTFT dropped to ~220ms, p99 at ~480ms. If they still want sub-200ms we should either push more aggressive fastpath thresholds or move to dedicated.
nana-sales: customer wants the next ramp in 15m. I'll coordinate. Also they're curious if we can temporarily raise their rate-limit for the next demo minute rather than moving to Dedicated.
sec-maya: can offer temporary rate-limit increase for demo if legal signs off; I'll loop in contracts.
deploy-bot: Incident created INC-20240211-092: queue-saturation-solstice; assigned to rachel-sre and peter-eng.
peter-eng: follow-up: I'll add a small TTL cache (60s) for identical small prompts and enable response-prefix caching at route level to further dampen load. Will keep an eye on eviction churn.
gina-solutions: I'll prepare a short quote and include a 14-day burst credit and an option for a minimal Dedicated reserve (2 GPUs) with SLA numbers.
nana-sales: thanks all 44d I'll post results after the next ramp.
kevin-support: note for playbook: for small-token fanout workloads, prefer fastpath + small batch caps + prefix prefill.
